texts: When the truncus divides into the aorta and the pulmonary artery, the sixth arches remain connected to the pulmonary trunk: B.
The front (ventral) parts of both sixth arches become the proximal right and left pulmonary arteries.
The back (dorsal) part of the LEFT sixth arch becomes the ductus arteriosus, joining the pulmonary trunk to the aorta; the dorsal part of the right sixth arch disappears.
So the normal ductus comes from the left sixth arch, and the distal pulmonary arteries grow from the lung buds, not from the arches.
In the picture, both sixth hoops stay with the money pipe, and only the back of the left one turns into the duct-tape tunnel.
Memory hook: the sixth hoops stay with the money; the left one's back is the duct.
